assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration opened a door that electron microscopists had waited on since Scherzer's 1936 theorem: routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects, and individual atoms. It is an invention verified by direct demonstration and now used across physics, materials science and chemistry. It fits the mandate for a discovery or invention that lets us see what could not be seen before.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the corrector design and electron-optical theory, Haider led the build and the first working TEM corrector with Urban's group, and Urban's group applied it to atomic-resolution materials work. These are three distinct, well-documented contributions that fit a three-person prize. Contributions from Rose, Haider and Urban may be entangled with the earlier STEM corrector work of others (e.g. Krivanek, Dellby), which the supplied credit leaves out.
assessment.maturity: The first demonstrations date from the late 1990s, and independent confirmation is overwhelming, with commercial aberration-corrected instruments installed worldwide. The impact has long been established, so recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the separate STEM aberration-correction line (Krivanek and collaborators) must be recognised alongside the TEM corrector for a fair allocation of credit.

Whether the committee regards electron-optical instrumentation as a physics discovery or invention under Nobel's will, since the 1986 Ruska prize is a precedent but chemistry and materials fields are the main users.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created an entirely new, tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean carbon system. The experimental discovery in 2018 followed the 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction. It has spawned a major field in moire quantum materials, so importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental observations of correlated insulating states and superconductivity. Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands, which guided the search. Allocation among the three is fairly clean, though the Cao et al. first author (Yuan Cao) is not creditable here and others (e.g. Dean, Young, Efetov, Ashoori) made major early confirmations.
assessment.maturity: The 2018 discovery has been replicated by many independent groups, and the correlated phases are well established, though the superconducting mechanism is still debated. At about eight years, recognition is somewhat early, but the experimental core is solid.
uncertainties: The mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved, so only the discovery of the phases can be recognised.
Credit for the experiment extends beyond the senior author to the first author and student team, which a three-person limit cannot reflect.
Other experimental groups with early independent results may compete for credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in 1995 and giant TMR in coherent MgO junctions around 2004 made magnetic read heads and MRAM practical, and led to dense storage in everyday devices. These are experimental discoveries with direct benefit to society. They follow from the spin-valve work already honoured in 2007 and are a natural successor.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995, which is a clean original-experiment claim that I would want to check carefully in the record. Parkin (and Yuasa et al. at AIST) reported giant MgO TMR in 2004, so the credit for the MgO step is shared with Yuasa and Djayaprawira, who are not on the list. Parkin's broader contribution to the industrial realisation is large.
assessment.maturity: The 1995 and 2004 results have been confirmed many times and are widely commercialised, so maturity is high and the recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether Parkin or the AIST group (Yuasa) holds the first MgO result; I cannot settle this from memory and the list omits Yuasa.
Overlap with the 2007 Nobel Prize for GMR may count against a second spintronics prize.
The compound discovery of Fe/Al2O3 TMR and MgO TMR may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and demonstration, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. They enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy, and a likely redefinition of the second. This is an instrument that opens a door to measurements that could not be made before.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme in 2001-2003 and first demonstrated it with strontium, which is the original idea and experiment. Ye's group brought the clocks to record accuracy and stability and demonstrated millikelvin-level gravitational redshift effects in the sample. A two-person prize is clean and gives fair credit, although others (e.g. Takamoto, Lemonde, Hall's frequency-comb partners) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and surpassed the performance, and the results are stable. Recognition is mature, with the redefinition of the second pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize for the frequency comb and with ion clocks (Wineland 2012) may affect the committee's appetite.
Ye also appears in the thorium clock candidate, which could complicate any plan of recognising him twice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the final piece of the Standard Model, which is a landmark of understanding the universe. The experiments rely on detector and instrument innovations that are themselves a major invention. The 2013 prize went to the theorists, and the experimental confirmation remains unrecognised.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the founding spokespersons and leaders of CMS and ATLAS and drove the detector concepts. Their credit is for leadership of collaborations of thousands, so I would want to be certain that the committee can defend the choice of three over the collaborations. The statutes limit the prize to three persons, and prior large-collaboration decisions complicate any single configuration.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been confirmed with more than a decade of data, with properties measured and consistent with the Standard Model. Recognition is mature.
uncertainties: The proposed persons are not the people who did the discovery analyses, so this is recognition of detector leadership instead of the discovery itself.
Whether the committee can fairly choose among collaboration leaders and other key physicists (e.g. Gianotti and Incandela, the discovery-era spokespersons) is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Lorimer burst in 2007 revealed a new class of extragalactic millisecond radio transients. Fast radio bursts have since become a probe of the intergalactic medium and the baryon census, with a local magnetar source (SGR 1935+2154) identified. This is an original observational discovery that opened a new field.
assessment.attribution: Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes published the 2007 discovery in archival Parkes pulsar data, and the second step of recognising a population was by Thornton et al. in 2013, which the credit leaves out. The first-observer credit is reasonably clear, although the finding came from a student-led data search (Lorimer's team and the Parkes archive, with Narkevic as the original finder), which complicates it.
assessment.maturity: The population is well established by CHIME, ASKAP and other facilities, with localisations to host galaxies. The physical origin is partly understood, so maturity is moderate, but the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Not all FRBs necessarily share one origin, so the physics being rewarded is partly unresolved.
Credit may have to include Thornton, Narkevic or CHIME, which exceeds three names or is absent from the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of astrophysical neutrinos in 2013 and the 2018 association with the blazar TXS 0506+056, plus the Galactic plane map, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. It is an instrument-driven discovery that gives a new window on cosmic accelerators.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the IceCube concept and its scientific programme, and Spiering was a central figure in the AMANDA and Baikal-era work and in IceCube. Prize credit would properly recognise the founding visionaries, but the discovery was made by a collaboration of hundreds and earlier pioneers (e.g. Baikal, DUMAND, AMANDA) bear on the allocation of credit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed, and source identification is promising, but the sources are not fully identified. Recognition is arguably early.
uncertainties: Individual blazar and Galactic source evidence may still strengthen, so the full impact is not yet clear.
Credit for the detector concept and the discovery analysis is spread across a large collaboration and predecessors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2013 experimental observation of quantised Hall conductance without a magnetic field in magnetic topological insulator films realised a long-sought phase and demonstrates dissipationless edge transport. It is a clean experiment that was verified, and it is relevant to metrology and low-power electronics, though temperatures remain very low.
assessment.attribution: Xue's group made the experimental observation. Fang and Dai, with colleagues, made the 2010 theoretical prediction of the magnetic-doped Bi2Se3-family candidate, which guided the experiment. Haldane's 1988 model is the foundational theory, and I note that Haldane has already been recognised in 2016. The three-person configuration is plausible, but Chang, Cui-Zu and others on the experiment (including the Stanford and Penn State groups) deserve consideration.
assessment.maturity: The result has been reproduced by other groups (e.g. at Stanford and Wurzburg), and quantisation precision has improved. Practical operation temperatures are low, so applications are still early, but the physical discovery is well verified.
uncertainties: Whether a prize should honour the experiment, the prediction, or both is not clear, and the attribution among the experimental team is complicated.
The competing topological insulator candidates (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) overlap and may be a better fit to a single prize.
